sn35.146:1.1: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you new and old kamma, the cessation of kamma, and the way leading to the cessation of kamma.
sn35.146:1.2: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak….
sn35.146:1.4: The eye is old kamma, to be seen as generated and fashioned by volition, as something to be felt.
sn35.146:1.6: The mind is old kamma, to be seen as generated and fashioned by volition, as something to be felt.
sn35.146:1.9: Whatever action one does now by body, speech, or mind.
sn35.146:1.11: “And what, bhikkhus, is the cessation of kamma?
sn35.146:1.12: When one reaches liberation through the cessation of bodily action, verbal action, and mental action,
sn35.146:1.13: this is called the cessation of kamma.
sn35.146:1.14: “And what, bhikkhus, is the way leading to the cessation of kamma?
sn35.146:1.15: It is this Noble Eightfold Path; that is,
sn35.146:1.16: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
sn35.146:1.18: I have taught old kamma, I have taught new kamma, I have taught the cessation of kamma, I have taught the way leading to the cessation of kamma.
sn35.146:1.19: Whatever should be done, bhikkhus, by a compassionate teacher out of compassion for his disciples, desiring their welfare, that I have done for you.
sn35.146:1.20: These are the feet of trees, bhikkhus, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent, lest you regret it later. This is our instruction to you.”
